original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cech-complex}
Let $\tau \in \{fppf, syntomic, smooth, \etale, Zariski\}$.
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$, or on
$S_\tau$ in case $\tau = \etale$, and let
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a standard $\tau$-covering of this site.
Let $V = \coprod_{i \in I} U_i$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $V$ is an affine scheme,
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{V \to U\}$ is an fpqc covering
and also a $\tau$-covering unless $\tau = Zariski$,
\item the {\v C}ech complexes
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$ and
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})$ agree.
\end{enumerate}

final_content.statement:
Fix a scheme $S$. The **big $\tau$-site** $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is a small-universe-selected category of $S$-schemes with covering families of type $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{Zariski}\}$. The **small étale site** $S_{\acute etale}$ has as objects étale $S$-schemes and as covers jointly surjective étale families; the **small Zariski site** $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ has open subschemes as objects. These are different sites; restriction from a big to a small site is not an identity of categories. For an abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on a site, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal F)$ denotes the $p$-th right derived functor of its sections over the site object $U$. A *standard $\tau$-cover of an affine $U$* is a **finite** jointly surjective family of affine maps $U_i\to U$, each flat finitely presented for fppf, standard syntomic, standard smooth, étale, or standard principal-open immersion, respectively.

For a site $\mathcal C$ and a family $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}$ with its iterated fibre products, an abelian presheaf $\mathcal F$ has a Čech cochain complex $\check C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{(i_0,\dots,i_q)}\mathcal F(U_{i_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{i_q})$, **including repeated indices**, with alternating restriction differential. For a sheaf $\mathcal F$, a positive-degree class in $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ becomes zero on a suitable cover because sheaf cohomology is obtained from injective resolutions and local exactness.

For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, let $\mathcal F^a$ be the induced abelian sheaf on a big scheme site: $\mathcal F^a(T\xrightarrow f S)=\Gamma(T,f^*\mathcal F)$, and restrict to the small étale site when appropriate. $H^p_{\mathrm{Zar}}(S,\mathcal F)$ is ordinary sheaf cohomology on the *topological space* $S$; it is not defined using all $S$-schemes.

Let $\tau \in \{fppf, syntomic, smooth, \mathrm{\acute etale}, Zariski\}$.
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_\tau$, or on
$S_\tau$ in case $\tau = \mathrm{\acute etale}$, and let
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
be a standard $\tau$-covering of this site.
Let $V = \coprod_{i \in I} U_i$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $V$ is an affine scheme,
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{V \to U\}$ is an fpqc covering
and also a $\tau$-covering unless $\tau = Zariski$,
\item the {\v C}ech complexes
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})$ and
$\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})$ agree.
\end{enumerate}

**Precise scope:** Finite disjoint unions of affine sources V are affine. The singleton V→U is fpqc; it is also τ-cover for τ≠Zariski, while in the **Zariski** case it generally is not a covering in that site. The natural refinement map of Čech complexes is a **degreewise isomorphism for sheaves** because F preserves disjoint coproducts as products. Never extend this claim to arbitrary presheaves.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-locality-cohomology}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site, $\mathcal{F}$ an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$,
$U$ an object of $\mathcal{C}$, $p > 0$ an integer and $\xi \in
H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$. Then there exists a covering
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ of $U$ in $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\xi |_{U_i} = 0$ for all $i \in I$.
